summary: Intermittent synchronous request timeouts for very long-context prompts (large max_tokens)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 504/timeout errors for synchronous (non-streaming) requests when using very large max_tokens and long prefix contexts. Failures appear initially as client-side 504s after ~90-120s.

Impact:
- NimbusHealth production integration experiences ~2-5% request failures on nightly batch jobs that send long clinical-context prompts (combined prefix ~120k tokens, max_tokens=8192).
- Affects time-sensitive document generation workflows; customer flagged as enterprise with SLA.

Environment / scope:
- Environment: prod us-east (us-east-1)
- Models observed: redwood/gpt-13b-quant (primary), open-llama-13b (fallback)
- Integration pattern: synchronous API calls (no streaming) called from customer backend with retry logic.
- Recent changes: Customer upgraded to quantized model two weeks ago; no Redwood-side config changes noted in same window.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Construct prompt with combined prefix ~120k tokens (tokenized by our tokenizer) consisting of multiple patient notes and system instructions.
2) Call /v1/generate with max_tokens=8192, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95, stream=false.
3) Observe 504 or connection terminated after ~90-120s intermittently (~1 in 20 requests).

Observed behavior:
- Request sometimes succeeds but often returns a 504 gateway timeout from API gateway.
- When request fails, there is no partial output returned; client sees immediate HTTP 504 with no body.
- On some failed attempts, service logs show the request making it to serving-runtime but an upstream worker dropped the connection during finalization.

Expected behavior:
- Request should either stream partial output or complete successfully within SLA, or return a structured error with model-level failure (5xx) if backend out of resources.

Initial hypothesis:
1) Large max_tokens combined with huge prefix increases KV cache memory usage and triggers aggressive eviction or background compaction; eviction leads to recompute that pushes worker beyond per-request finalization timeout.
2) Synchronous (non-streaming) requests create larger per-request buffering at the API gateway and LB that hits internal connection timeouts.
3) Quantized kernel path for redwood/gpt-13b-quant has intermittent stalls at very large output lengths causing the worker to stop responding to health pings.

Logs / artifacts attached by customer:
- Sample request ID: req-20260310-90a7b
- Customer-provided client logs (included): client_request.log (shows HTTP 504s and retry timestamps)
- Server-side trace: internal trace link: https://observability.redwood/trace/req-20260310-90a7b

Workaround suggested to customer initially:
- Reduce max_tokens to 4096 and/or split prompt into two sequential requests.
- Use streaming=true to allow partial result delivery and lower API gateway buffer pressure.

Customer impact and urgency:
- Customer requests priority investigation due to nightly batch job SLAs. They can tolerate short-term workaround but want long-term fix for large single-request use cases.

investigation_notes: Correlated traces and host metrics show: 1) KV cache eviction spikes during token generation when prefix > ~100k tokens; eviction causes recompute that significantly increases finalization time. 2) Quantized kernel path (used by redwood/gpt-13b-quant) exhibits a per-token tail latency increase for large sequence lengths compared to non-quantized FP16 path. 3) API gateway default idle timeout at 120s contributed to client-facing 504s when worker finalizer exceeded that window. Reproducible in internal staging with a synthetic prompt matching token counts. Hypothesis validated: combined effect of eviction-triggered recompute + quantized tail-latency pushed end-to-end beyond gateway timeout intermittently.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: applied customer-scoped routing to prefer non-quantized model variant for NimbusHealth and bumped API gateway idle timeout to 180s for their tenant. This reduced failures to acceptable levels for nightly jobs. Long-term remediation planned: 1) Runtime change to reduce KV eviction noise for extremely long prefixes (adjust compaction thresholds and pre-eviction heuristics). 2) Kernel optimization work to address quantized tail-latency at long sequence lengths (tracked in PR 1284). 3) Add an alert on kv_eviction_rate and worker_finalizer_latency for high-prefix workloads and a documented runbook entry for handling long-sync requests. Follow-ups: ENG-OPS task to add tenant routing automation and PROD rollout of kernel fix (estimate 2 sprints).
